facts.raw_span: born at 35 weeks 4 days’ gestation
weighing 2152 g
one of monochorionic diamniotic twins
her identical twin died in utero at 24 weeks
Fetal ultrasound had shown microcephaly and ventricular enlargement
Postnatal MRI of the head revealed microcephaly, marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles without signs of elevated intracranial pressure
severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
the temporal lobes, basal ganglia, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum were preserved
No intracranial hematoma or neoplastic lesions were seen
very weak light reflexes bilaterally
mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign
No chorioretinal dysplasia was noted

concepts.why: The combination of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes, along with the presence of mild optic nerve pallor and suspected peripapillary double-ring sign, suggests a diagnosis of Fetal akinesia deformation sequence.
The presence of ventricular enlargement and microcephaly, along with the absence of intracranial hematoma or neoplastic lesions, supports a diagnosis of Congenital hydrocephalus.
The presence of very weak light reflexes bilaterally and mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign suggests a diagnosis of Optic nerve hypoplasia.

The combination of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes, along with the preservation of the temporal lobes, basal ganglia, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum, suggests a diagnosis of Cerebral dysgenesis.
The presence of monochorionic diamniotic twins and the death of one twin in utero suggests a diagnosis of Monochorionic twin pregnancy complications.
It explains the finding of weak light reflexes and optic nerve pallor in the absence of chorioretinal dysplasia.

rationales.F03: Monochorionic diamniotic twins are at increased risk for complications such as twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome, which can lead to fetal akinesia deformation sequence and cerebral dysgenesis.
rationales.F04: The death of one twin in utero can lead to complications for the surviving twin, including cerebral dysgenesis and monochorionic twin pregnancy complications.
rationales.F05: Microcephaly and ventricular enlargement are characteristic features of fetal akinesia deformation sequence and congenital hydrocephalus.
rationales.F10: Weak light reflexes can be a sign of optic nerve hypoplasia or Leber congenital amaurosis.
rationales.F11: Mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign is a characteristic feature of optic nerve hypoplasia.

frontier_selector.rationale: The combination of monochorionic diamniotic twins, the death of one twin in utero, and the observed brain abnormalities in the surviving twin support the champion diagnosis, with cerebral dysgenesis being a possible contributing factor to the observed microcephaly and ventricular enlargement.
